answer: A bond-backed identity vault makes fake agents expensive: each agent locks a stake in a shared vault before it can trade, and that stake is slashed if peers prove it cheated. A long horizon helps — the bond vests slowly, so a Sybil farm must fund every identity for months before it can profit. Like light through a prism, one identity is one beam: splitting a stake across many fakes dilutes each one below the trust threshold. Attack cost scales with every fake.
